articles.title: UGV or robot dog for industrial inspection: a practical comparison
articles.excerpt: By the engineering team at YUANZHI ROBOTICS. We design and build sensor payloads for robot dogs, UGVs and drones. Originally published on our site; AI-assisted draft, reviewed by our engineers. The qu…
articles.body: By the engineering team at YUANZHI ROBOTICS. We design and build sensor payloads for robot dogs, UGVs and drones. Originally published on our site; AI-assisted draft, reviewed by our engineers. The question comes up in almost every inspection project: should the sensors ride on a wheeled or tracked vehicle, or on a legged robot? Both are now mature enough to run unattended rounds. This guide compares them on the points that decide a project in practice: the route, the payload, runtime and speed, weather and protection, cost and upkeep, and what changes in the sensor payload between the two. We build payloads for both and have no preference beyond fitting the site.
articles.author: YUANZHI ROBOTICS

articles.body: OpenAI's new funding round is reportedly raising less than planned. TechCrunch summarised reporting from the Financial Times and the Wall Street Journal, and the details below come from that summary. OpenAI had not commented when it was published; TechCrunch said it had asked the company. What was reported Earlier reports put the raise at $30 billion, first at a $1.4 trillion valuation and later at $1.25 trillion, ahead of a planned IPO. The Financial Times reported on Friday that the target is now $20 billion, and that the first close is expected to come in below that figure. A group of investors from the United Arab Emirates is expected to lead the round. A later retail offering aimed at wealthy individuals could lift the total to the $20 billion target.

articles.title: Deterministic Runtime Governance: Moving from Paper Compliance to Machine Reality (BIGF)
articles.excerpt: In traditional enterprise IT, governance follows a broken rhythm: developers push code, and compliance teams check Word documents once a year during an audit. When things go wrong in production, organ…
articles.body: In traditional enterprise IT, governance follows a broken rhythm: developers push code, and compliance teams check Word documents once a year during an audit. When things go wrong in production, organizations scramble to schedule an emergency meeting while systems degrade. Implementing the Business Impact Governance Framework (BIGF) replaces subjective human triage with deterministic runtime enforcement across four core operational phases. Phase 1: Policy-as-Code — Transforming Compliance into Machine Reality Statutory mandates (such as DORA, NIS2, or the EU AI Act) and internal Business Impact Analysis (BIA) baselines are translated directly into machine-executable parameters. This is not a policy manual for a committee.
articles.author: Erkki Laine

articles.title: Light the Candle: An Offline Día de los Muertos Ofrenda Builder
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine Ofrenda is a private, offline remembrance builder for Día de los Muertos. You enter a loved one's name,…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built Ofrenda is a private, offline remembrance builder for Día de los Muertos. You enter a loved one's name, your relationship, their favorite foods and songs, and a memory. A local open weight model then writes three things: a short remembrance honoring them, a gentle "letter back" in a warm voice, and a list of items to place on your ofrenda. It all appears on a candlelit, marigold themed page. I read the theme "Ghost in the Machine" as the people who live on in our stories. On Día de los Muertos, the line between past and present gets thinner, and the machine here isn't haunted. It helps carry a memory forward.

articles.title: A PKCS#11 key can be protected and still be over-authorized
articles.excerpt: A PKCS#11 key can be protected and still be over-authorized Moving a signing key into an HSM changes where the key material lives. It does not automatically decide which application, workload, or oper…
articles.body: A PKCS#11 key can be protected and still be over-authorized Moving a signing key into an HSM changes where the key material lives. It does not automatically decide which application, workload, or operator may use that key for a particular purpose. PKCS#11 provides object attributes and authentication controls, but the security result depends on how an application exposes those controls. The PKCS#11 specification describes attributes such as CKA_SIGN , CKA_DECRYPT , CKA_SENSITIVE , and CKA_EXTRACTABLE . These restrict operations on a key object. CKA_ALWAYS_AUTHENTICATE can require the user to supply a PIN for each use of a private key. The setting is useful for higher-assurance signing, but it does not establish that the requested operation is authorized for the business transaction.
articles.author: Ioneyrezende

articles.title: FHIR Validation Doesn't Tell You What to Do Next, So I Built a Decision Layer
articles.excerpt: A FHIR resource can pass validation and still be the wrong thing to act on. I built a small decision layer for that gap: it takes parsed FHIR R4 resources, sends a flattened state to TypeSafe AI's Jev…
articles.body: A FHIR resource can pass validation and still be the wrong thing to act on. I built a small decision layer for that gap: it takes parsed FHIR R4 resources, sends a flattened state to TypeSafe AI's Jev model, and turns the answer into accept, route, flag or human review. On 204 synthetic records, the first live run lost routing to my hand-written rules, 0.814 to 0.922, and missed too many notifiable diseases. Both failures came from my own setup. One was a serializer bug and the other was a badly framed routing question. After fixing both, Jev scored above the rules on all three decisions, on the same records. It still misses my latency target by a wide margin. This is a proof of concept. It runs on synthetic data and it is not connected to any production system.
articles.author: Budi Widhiyanto

articles.excerpt: Sir Patrick Stewart is being remembered for Star Trek and X-Men, but he was also the perfect guest star on The Simpsons
articles.body: Yesterday, news broke that Sir Patrick Stewart died at age 86. With his background performing Shakespeare and his incredible sense of dignity and gravitas, Stewart is being celebrated primarily for his work as Captain Jean-Luc Picard on Star Trek: The Next Generation , as well as being the perfect man to portray Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films. But while he was beloved for the dramatic weight he brought to his roles, it's worth acknowledging that the man pulled off some incredibly memorable comedic performances, one of the first was on The Simpsons , where he guest-starred in the season 6 episode, “Homer the Great.”

articles.body: The best twist endings in video games change what you thought you were playing. A great one makes you want to start over to spot the clues, and a perfect one hides those clues in plain sight: in dialogue, in chapter titles, perhaps even the controller you’re holding. These ten games span three decades and nearly every genre, from horror to puzzle-platformers to a Game Boy adventure about a dream. But they all have one thing in common: Every one of them had us totally fooled the first time.

articles.excerpt: Grab your high-lumen flashlight and gargantuan gun to explore these vicious vessels
articles.body: Abandoned, possessed, or infested spaceships in sci-fi films, books, and video games are usually not a welcoming place to hang your helmet and kick back inside. Many are distinctly marked as DO NOT APPROACH zones and equipped with clearly articulated warning messages to keep your distance, but that doesn't ever seem to stop scavengers, space pirates, or evil industrial mega corporations from waving off these dangerous signs to board anyway. Other creaky craft are apt to contain nasty alien hitchhikers or biological hazards not exactly conducive to a pleasant star-trekking voyage. Whether these nefarious neglected craft have just reappeared from the other side of a black hole or have been lying dormant for eons on a hostile planetoid, visitors are usually infrequent.

articles.body: On Episode 234 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Mike Wall are joined by Than Putzig of the Planetary Science Institute about a NASA-backed payload bound for the Marius Hills Pit on the moon. In our ongoing quest to develop a moon base, could we possibly utilize the area beneath the surface of the moon in order to make the moon habitable? Could Marius Hills Pit, a roughly 50-meter-wide opening that may lead into a lunar lava tube, become the Moon's first living habitat for humans? Putzig explains how geophysical instruments on a rover could detect hidden voids beneath the surface and measure the size of these lava tubes.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
articles.excerpt: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. Here's why it was so creepy.
articles.body: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

articles.title: The moon, Mars, and Jupiter shine in the heart of the Lion overnight on Nov. 1-2
articles.excerpt: The waning moon shines with Jupiter, Mars and the brilliant star Regulus in the eastern sky overnight Nov. 1-2.
articles.body: The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know. Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky. Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer .

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
